claim_boundary: Frank rejected the complete Phase C set on 2026-08-24 because it varied surface rendering rather than the requested robot morphology. The historical scores below are preserved only to document why maker scoring cannot substitute for founder judgment or a correctly framed experiment.

candidates.strongest: Best overall warm-competence balance; feels institutional and authored rather than technological by default.
candidates.weakest: Painted background and chest accent need a tighter reusable grammar across fifty agents.

candidates.strongest: Most credible operational profile language; precise, calm, legible, and easy to connect to real agent documentation.
candidates.weakest: Less ownable at first glance than the strongest print directions unless role-specific mark-making is systematized.

candidates.strongest: Highest small-crop recognition and a highly scalable spot-color system.
candidates.weakest: Large geometric fields can read as campaign art and overwhelm the quieter governance promise.

candidates.strongest: Friendly tactile ink overlap with authentic independent-publishing character.
candidates.weakest: Trend and zine associations may reduce enterprise maturity, and the coral optic can overstate emotional activity.

candidates.strongest: Strongest Academy and .org specimen language; calm, inspectable, archival, and trustworthy.
candidates.weakest: Low contrast weakens thumbnail distinction and it overlaps visually with pen-and-wash.

candidates.strongest: Only candidate that directly visualizes inspectability and how a specialist might work.
candidates.weakest: Invented internal machinery is expensive to keep canonical; the red module could be mistaken for a battery, hazard, or weapon component.

candidates.strongest: Most ownable icon and strongest profile-card silhouette; feels public-minded, tactile, and memorable.
candidates.weakest: The heavy black field is less suited to subtle runtime-state expression and can become campaign-like if overused.

candidates.strongest: Accessible story tone and a feasible bridge into Academy motion sequences.
candidates.weakest: This export remains too close to watercolor illustration to justify a distinct canonical style.

candidates.strongest: Ownable modular material metaphor; warmth comes from construction rather than a cute face.
candidates.weakest: Background layers are busy in profile contexts and consistent depth across a large agent portfolio will require strict templates.

candidates.strongest: Warmest physical presence and a strong route for story stills, exhibitions, or Academy sequences.
candidates.weakest: Workbench context may imply a toy or prototype, and photoreal continuity across many agents is costly.

recommendation.do_not_continue: Do not place any Phase C candidate into production UI or audience testing.
recommendation.lesson: Hold identity and role constant, but vary silhouette, proportion, locomotion, body architecture, face logic, material system, and performance before comparing rendering media.
